newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended down on Tuesday as they failed to convincingly recover from an early wave of futures-selling that followed through from late trade on Monday, dealers said.
Futures traders dumped stock in a quietish market whose nerves are still frayed by last week's mauling at the hands of the ailing rand. Industrial stocks bore the brunt of the losses.
"The downside was nearly all futures-related," one dealer said.

Positive data from South Africa's producer price index (PPI) provided some support to haul shares off their day lows, but the index never fully regained its early losses. The PPI data came in slightly better than expected.
The all-share index lost 28.9 points to end at 6,924.0 and the industrials index shed 26.9 points to close at 8,148.4.
Dealers said the market ignored comments by finance minister Trevor Manuel that South Africa may retain a "modicum" of exchange controls.
Market eyes are watching for a firm indication as to when controls will be scrapped, but Manuel gave no details of a timetable.

Dealers said the market would look to Wall Street's performance for overnight guidance, but that signals may not be clear as New York markets hang nervously on the results of Tuesday's national elections.
"For industrials it all depends on what happens on Wall Street," one dealer said.
The golds index fared better and rose 7.6 points to 1,740.1 as the bullion price steadied, but dealers said the recent strong performance of the gold shares was starting to look vulnerable.
"They have been going well and I think they could well come off a bit tomorrow (Wednesday)," one said.

Most blue chips ended the day slightly down as Anglo lost 125 cents to 279.75 rand, SA Breweries dropped 75 cents to 120.75 and Iscor, attracting heavy trade of 2.28 million shares, lost five cents to 329.
One bright spot was the steep rise in price of Lyndenburg Exploration Ltd whose stock jumped more than 50 percent to close at 13.10 rand, up 4440 cents.

The jump was spurred as trade in its shares resumed after a suspension announced when Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd bought a 44.8 percent slice of the group. The deal valued Lydex paper at about 14 rand a share.

After the initial bout of selling futures ended the day quietly with the December all-share contract at 6,370/85 from 6,380 and industrials at 7,858/65 from 7,860. The golds contract was stronger at 1,247/52 from 1,239.
